label: token i fed back early in the copy phase (as copied token 0, or token 1 in short sequences)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is i, almost entirely in the copy phase (99.5% of mass), where the fed-back i is an early original token. It fires most strongly at the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, input = original token 0 = i). That case holds 87% of the mass, and every top example is a sequence starting with i, near max activation. Weaker activations come from i fed back at recall_idx 2 (original token 1 = i), and these fade as L grows: frequent for L<=6, rare for L>=7. It does not fire on any other token, at the delimiter, or on i during the original phase except for a trace at orig_idx 4-6 where i repeats an earlier token (in_first=0). It also does not fire on i fed back at recall_idx >= 3.

issues: The main claims hold up. The feature fires only on input i (100% of mass), 99.5% of the mass is in the copy phase, recall_idx 1 carries 87% and recall_idx 2 carries 12%, and it never fires at the delimiter.

Systematic false positives at recall_idx 1 for L=9: precision of i & copy & recall_idx==1 & L==9 is only 0.243 (n=2792) on test. For L=3..7 it is about 1.0 and for L=8 it is 0.909. The test-split misses output shows this directly: many inactive *i* at step 10, all from L=9 sequences starting with i. The explanation says the fade with L applies only to recall_idx 2, but it also applies to recall_idx 1.

The claim that recall_idx 2 fires 'frequently for L<=6' is too coarse. Test precision at recall_idx 2 by L: L=3 0.316, L=4 0.943, L=5 0.975, L=6 0.696, L=7 0.128, L=8 0.005, L=9 0.001. L=3 is mostly inactive, so the window is roughly L 4-6, not L<=6.

There is a small uncovered class at recall_idx 3 for L=4: test precision 0.196 over 2446 steps. The explanation says it never fires at recall_idx >= 3, which is wrong, though the mass here is tiny (0.4%).
The trace activity in the original phase at orig_idx 4-6 is confirmed (0.5% of mass) and is negligible.
skeptic.revised_label: token i fed back at the start of the copy phase: as copied token 0 (L<=8; mostly silent at L=9), or as copied token 1 for mid-length sequences (L 4-6)
